Case plans are designed, implemented and continually revisited to address barriers to self\-sufficiency and to encourage and support clients in securing appropriate public social services benefits and/or employment, mental and physical health care, appropriate housing and a variety of other individualized services.

**Position Title:** Housing Navigator

**Department:** Homelessness Initiatives

**Report To:** Program Supervisor

**Type:** Full Time, Non\-Exempt, Regular

**Date Revised:**  August 2026

**ABOUT US:**

United Way is advancing the common good in Ventura County by providing help today in ways that strengthen tomorrow. United Way has the scope, expertise and influences to bring together human services agencies, government, businesses, private foundations and dedicated volunteers around a common vision of creating maximum impact and achieving long\-lasting results. Why United Way? We all want to have the greatest possible impact on our community and the issues that we care about. Join the movement. At United Way, you unite your hopes and strengths with others to accomplish more than any of us can alone.

**ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW:**The mission of the United Way of Ventura County is: “To Mobilize and Inspire the Caring Power and Resources of our Community.” In keeping with this charge and in response to the shelter crisis in Ventura County, the United Way of Ventura County has launched a Homelessness Initiative to include a Landlord Engagement Program (LEP) to increase housing stock and utilize existing housing vouchers and housing subsidies provided by local jurisdictions and community partners in preventing and ending homelessness. Everyone needs a safe place to call home, yet that basic need is increasingly out of reach for many people in Ventura County. Limited affordable housing supply, extremely low vacancy rates, and prohibitive and rising rents, make home access for those with housing barriers exceedingly challenging. Advocating for these individuals and families includes recruiting, cultivating, retaining, and growing the number of landlords willing to help prevent and end homelessness.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Housing Navigator position provides direct client support to assist individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. This role is responsible for conducting client intakes, determining program eligibility, collecting and verifying documentation, maintaining accurate case records, and connecting clients to housing and community resources. The position also assists with housing navigation activities, landlord engagement, outreach, lease\-up coordination, and ongoing housing retention efforts. Working closely with case managers, community partners, and property owners, this role helps ensure clients receive timely, coordinated, and person\-centered services while supporting the organization’s mission to promote housing stability and prevent homelessness. This is a grant\-funded position and may only be temporary employment unless other grants can continue to support the position.

**Intake Duties:**

· Conduct initial intake interviews with clients to gather demographic, financial, and personal information.

· Explain program eligibility requirements, services, and client rights and responsibilities.

· Collect, verify, and organize required documentation (e.g., identification, income, housing, benefits).

· Enter and maintain client information in case management systems, including HMIS, Apricot, and internal databases, while ensuring data accuracy and confidentiality.

· Screen clients for program eligibility and assess immediate needs, barriers, and service goals.

· Provide appropriate referrals and connections to community resources, supportive services, and other programs when clients are not eligible or require additional assistance.

· Maintain compliance with program policies, funding requirements, confidentiality standards, and documentation procedures.

**Case Management Support Duties:**

· Assist case managers with light caseload support such as scheduling appointments, follow\-up calls, and providing reminders to clients.

· Provide clients with referrals to community resources such as food banks, shelters, employment services, and healthcare providers.

· Support clients with applications for benefits or services under supervision of a case manager.

· Document client progress notes and updates in case files.

· Monitor and track client participation and program compliance.

· Assist with crisis intervention and problem\-solving when appropriate, escalating to case managers when necessary.

**Housing Navigation \& Outreach:**

* Landlord outreach and engagement. Build and maintain relationships with property owners, managers, and housing partners.
* Assist with outreach to community organizations (e.g. Neighborhood Councils, Faith Based Organizations, Apartment Owners Associations, Non\-profit Housing) to engage and educate the community and housing partners.
* Assist with lease\-up process, as needed.
* Assist with follow\-up to property owners after housing placement and continue communication with clients to ensure housing retention. Communicate with supervisor if the client has needs that you need assistance with including mental health emergency.

* Coordinate housing and homelessness\-related activities and communications with the County of Ventura, local organizations, and other homeless service providers.

United American Indian Involvement (UAII) is the only Urban Indian Organization in Los Angeles County, proudly serving as a home for American Indian and Alaska Native communities. Through our healthcare facility and culturally centered programs, we provide essential physical, behavioral, and spiritual health services—helping individuals stay connected to their Tribal heritage and traditions.

  

For over 50 years, UAII has grown to become the largest nonprofit provider of health and human services for American Indians and Alaska Natives in Los Angeles, home to the nation’s largest Urban Indian population. Our dedicated team delivers compassionate care that supports daily healing, resilience, and the continued strength of our communities. UAII is committed to uphold Indigenous values in all aspects of our work. It guides our actions, relationships, and responsibilities, ensuring that we serve our communities with integrity, respect, and accountability.

 **Core Principles**

* Respect for Relatives – I will honor the dignity of all people, recognizing that every individual is a relative deserving of respect, compassion, and care.
* Community Responsibility – My work is not only for individual benefit but for the collective well\-being of our communities, present and future.
* Cultural Integrity, I will safeguard and uplift Indigenous languages, traditions, and cultural practices, ensuring they remain central to our organizational life.
* Reciprocity We give back in balance with what we receive, fostering mutual trust and accountability in all relationships.
* Stewardship – I will act as a caretaker of our communities, resources, and environment, mindful of the impact of our decisions on future generations.
* Truth and Transparency – I will communicate honestly and openly, ensuring clarity in our commitments and accountability in our actions

jobs.title: Housing Navigator
jobs.description:
#### **DMH**

#### **JOB SUMMARY:**


The primary role of the Housing Navigator (HN) is to identify interim housing for the clients and participants in Weingart Center’s Programs and Services Department. The HN works directly with Case Managers (CM) and other service providers who have screened participants for housing. The HN is responsible for locating housing options, developing relationships with landlords and property management companies as well as facilitating the application process along with the CM and participant. They will assist the CM with housing selection, budgeting and finding needed supportive services in the community.



ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS INCLUDE, but are not limited to the following:



Works in conjunction with the Case Manager to provide an appropriate housing plan.



Accurately assesses each client’s/participant’s individual housing needs against housing resources.



Assists client/participant to secure appropriate housing.



Assists client/participant in completing housing applications, if needed.



Works with Case Manager throughout the housing application processes.



Assists client/participant in contacting and making tenant arrangements with prospective landlords.



Responsible for canvassing for housing resources in the community.



Helps client/participant to identify needed resources in the community in which participants choose to live.



Helps client/participant to complete and understand rental agreements and to explain thoroughly housing terms and conditions.



Provides specific information to client/participant regarding programs to obtain special utility rates for low\-income users.



Networks with affordable housing agencies in different communities.



Maintains current brochures, applications, and materials available to help ensure a client’s/participant’s successful transition.



Confers with supportive services staff on a regular basis to ensure client success in obtaining residential stability.



Other related duties as required.


#### **REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:**


Must be empathetic and have excellent listening skills.



Strong knowledge of low\-income housing resources, social service, welfare, legal, corrections, health care, substance abuse, alcoholism, mental health care, and other systems associated with target population.



Strong ability to advocate effectively on behalf of low\-income and/or homeless clients/participants.



Clear and complete speech and communication skills.



A valid California Driver License required.



Must have current automobile and liability insurance with reliable transportation.


#### **REQUIRED EDUCATION/TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:**


A bachelor’s degree in social services preferred, or two (2\) years of relevant social services experience.



Experience in the delivery of social services to homeless and/or low\-income individuals.



Demonstrated abilities in management of multiple projects and priorities essential.


#### **PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:**


Sitting and standing for long periods of time, walking, stooping, and bending.



Ability to move to various physical locations in the complex.



Ability to see, hear and talk clearly to receive instructions and to give instructions.



Complex reading skills, complex writing skills, judgment, and decision\-making capability.



Ability to be self\-directed in work and work well with others as part of a case\-work team.



Work indoors in a temperature\-controlled environment.



Ability to work well under highly stressful conditions, to interact with needy participants, to set realistic goals, to establish healthy boundaries.



Ability to respond effectively to the most sensitive inquiries or complaints.



High level concentration and attention to detail for extended periods of time required.



Ability to quickly organize and communicate thoughts and to understand communications from others.



Ability to work independently, with others and around others, to have verbal contact with others, face\-to\-face contact with others, and to prioritize work and make decisions.



Must be fully vaccinated against COVID\-19 as defined by CDC.


#### **About WEINGART CENTER ASSOCIATION**


As one of the best comprehensive human services organizations in the western United States, Weingart Center is committed to removing barriers that keep people from housing. With multiple Interim and Permanent Supportive Housing solutions throughout the greater Los Angeles area, Weingart Center addresses the needs of seniors, Veterans, women, members of the LGBTQAI\+ community, the formerly incarcerated, and many others experiencing homelessness. All Weingart Center housing solutions include comprehensive wraparound services, which are designed to help clients overcome challenges and clear the way for a fulfilling life.

Through our healthcare facility and culturally centered programs, we provide essential physical, behavioral, and spiritual health services—helping individuals stay connected to their Tribal heritage and traditions.

  

For over 50 years, UAII has grown to become the largest nonprofit provider of health and human services for American Indians and Alaska Natives in Los Angeles, home to the nation’s largest Urban Indian population. Our dedicated team delivers compassionate care that supports daily healing, resilience, and the continued strength of our communities. UAII is committed to uphold Indigenous values in all aspects of our work. It guides our actions, relationships, and responsibilities, ensuring that we serve our communities with integrity, respect, and accountability.

 **Core Principles**

* Respect for Relatives – I will honor the dignity of all people, recognizing that every individual is a relative deserving of respect, compassion, and care.
* Community Responsibility – My work is not only for individual benefit but for the collective well\-being of our communities, present and future.
* Cultural Integrity, I will safeguard and uplift Indigenous languages, traditions, and cultural practices, ensuring they remain central to our organizational life.
* Reciprocity We give back in balance with what we receive, fostering mutual trust and accountability in all relationships.
* Stewardship – I will act as a caretaker of our communities, resources, and environment, mindful of the impact of our decisions on future generations.
* Truth and Transparency – I will communicate honestly and openly, ensuring clarity in our commitments and accountability in our actions

**Position Summary**


Through culturally grounded wraparound services, UAII works to remove barriers to permanent housing and uplift individuals experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or severe rent burden throughout Los Angeles County. Under the general direction of the Housing Program Manager or CalAIM Project Lead, the Housing Case Manager (CalAIM) supports clients in securing safe and stable housing. This role provides individualized case management, assists with housing searches, and builds strong relationships with property owners, managers, and community partners to expand permanent and supportive housing opportunities.


The Housing Case Manager (CalAIM) collaborates closely with internal team members, provides essential administrative support, and utilizes all functions of the Los Angeles Continuum of Care (LAHSA/HMIS, CHAMP, DPSS, CBEST, LA DHS, LA DMH), as well as CDSS and CalAIM CS systems. This position plays a critical role in guiding clients toward housing stability and long\-term success within a compassionate, culturally attuned service environment.

**This is a grant funded position.**

*An individual in this role must be able to perform the following duties with or without reasonable accommodation. The tasks listed provide representative examples and may not include all responsibilities assigned.*

* Monitor and verify participant eligibility status throughout program enrollment(s).

* Develop and implement an Individualized Care Plan for participants based on the needs and barriers identified in the Initial Assessment.

* Assist participants with housing searches, housing placement, and ongoing tenancy support.
* Support participants in completing rental applications, subsidized housing and supportive housing paperwork; interpret and explain lease terms and educate on tenant rights and responsibilities.
* Conduct habitability home inspections and provide periodic home visits after housing placement.
* Mediate and advocate on behalf of participants with landlords, addressing disputes, payment arrangements, unit surrender, relocations, and other housing\-related issues.
* Collaborate closely with UAII Workforce Development, Behavioral Health, Wellness (SUD treatment), Clinic/Dental teams, and external community partners to provide comprehensive wraparound services.
* Develop and maintain an effective internal and external referral network to ensure timely warm handoffs and individualized participant support.
* Build partnerships with CoC agencies, property owners, property management companies, and agents to expand housing opportunities and promote long\-term housing stability.

The person in this position will be responsible for conducting pre\-release care coordination for justice\-involved individuals eligible for Enhanced Care Management (ECM) services under the CalAIM Justice\-Involved Initiative. The Justice\-Involved Pre\-Release Care Coordinator will conduct in\-reach activities within correctional facilities and coordinate care planning prior to release to ensure successful transition into community\-based services.

  

The Care Coordinator will work as part of a multi\-disciplinary care team including correctional health staff, behavioral health providers, managed care plans, and community providers to ensure continuity of care upon release. Responsibilities include outreach, eligibility verification, assessment, development of individualized care plans, and coordination of medical, behavioral health, housing, and social services to address the clinical and non\-clinical needs of justice\-involved Members. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:  

* Conduct in\-reach within correctional facilities to identify and engage justice\-involved individuals eligible for Enhanced Care Management services prior to release.
* Receive and review referrals from Medi\-Cal Managed Care Plans, correctional partners, and community agencies and determine eligibility for program participation.
* Conduct intake screenings and develop individualized pre\-release care plans in collaboration with the Member and multidisciplinary care team.
* Coordinate pre\-release discharge planning, including linkage to medical care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, housing resources, and other community\-based services.
* Collaborate with correctional health staff, managed care plans, probation/parole, and community providers to ensure continuity of care upon release.
* Assist Members with appointment scheduling, and other reentry needs.
* Manage an assigned caseload of Members, including maintaining accurate records and tracking program data.
* Provide service coordination and referrals to medical, behavioral health, housing, and community\-based providers, including follow\-up to ensure service connection.

* Provide services in a culturally responsive and linguistically appropriate manner.
* Embrace and embody the mission, vision, guiding principles, clinical vision, and goals of WestCare Foundation.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience and Competencies:

* Ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain detailed records.
* Bilingual preferred.

* Graduation with a two\-year degree in Addiction Counseling, Psychology, Social Work, Community and Human Services, Rehabilitation Counseling, or related field preferred.

LICENSURE/CERTIFICATION:

jobs.description:
About Empowering Success Now

Empowering Success Now (ESN) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to helping individuals and families overcome barriers, access resources, develop valuable skills, improve their well\-being, and create pathways toward long\-term success.

Our organization provides support through four primary service areas:

* **Mental Wellness**
* **Job Placement Assistance**
* **Community Resources**
* **Skills Training**

We believe that every client deserves individualized support, consistent follow\-up, and access to resources that can help them move forward.

Position Overview

Empowering Success Now is seeking an experienced, compassionate, organized, and community\-driven **Case Manager** to oversee and support client caseloads across our programs.

The Case Manager will serve as a central point of connection between our clients and ESN's different departments. This individual will help ensure clients are successfully connected to the services they need, remain engaged in their programs, receive appropriate follow\-up, and do not fall through the cracks.

The Case Manager will conduct client intakes, assess needs, coordinate services, schedule appointments, follow up with clients, maintain case records, track outcomes, advocate for clients, and collaborate with ESN program staff to ensure clients receive appropriate support.

Case Management Responsibilities

* Manage and monitor client caseloads across ESN's Mental Wellness, Job Placement Assistance, Community Resources, and Skills Training programs.
* Serve as a primary point of contact for clients navigating one or multiple ESN services.
* Conduct client intakes and gather information regarding the client's needs, goals, barriers, and requested services.
* Help determine which ESN program or services may best meet each client's needs.
* Connect clients with the appropriate ESN department, staff member, program, appointment, training, or resource.
* Schedule and coordinate client appointments and program bookings as needed.
* Maintain regular communication with clients through phone calls, email, text, appointments, and other approved communication methods.
* Follow up with clients to ensure they received the services or resources they were connected to.
* Monitor client participation and progress throughout ESN programs.
* Re\-engage clients who miss appointments, become inactive, or stop participating before completing services.
* Motivate and encourage clients to continue utilizing services that can help them achieve their goals.
* Identify additional needs or barriers that may arise during a client's participation and connect them with appropriate resources.
* Advocate for clients when they need assistance navigating services, organizations, programs, or community resources.
* Assist individual departments with their caseloads when additional support is needed.
* Conduct periodic client check\-ins to determine whether additional services are needed.
* Follow up with clients after services are completed to determine outcomes and whether additional assistance is necessary.
* Help clients transition out of services appropriately once their needs have been met.
* Maintain professional boundaries and protect confidential client information.

Documentation, Data \& Grant Support

Accurate documentation is an important part of this position because ESN uses program data to understand its impact and meet reporting requirements.

The Case Manager will:

* Maintain accurate, organized, and timely client files and case notes.
* Document client contacts, appointments, referrals, services provided, participation, progress, and outcomes.
* Maintain updated client rosters and caseload information across departments.
* Track client enrollment, participation, completion, referrals, and other program outcomes.
* Assist with collecting accurate program numbers and statistics needed for grant reporting.
* Help identify success stories, program outcomes, service numbers, and other information needed to demonstrate program impact.
* Work with program staff to ensure client information and program outcomes are being documented consistently.
* Assist with preparing internal reports and information requested by leadership.
* Maintain confidentiality and follow organizational policies regarding client information and records.

Client Advocacy \& Resource Navigation

* Build trusting and professional relationships with clients from diverse backgrounds.
* Listen to clients' needs and help identify practical next steps.
* Advocate for clients while encouraging clients to become confident advocates for themselves.
* Research community resources when ESN cannot directly provide a requested service.
* Connect clients with appropriate outside organizations and service providers.
* Help clients understand available programs, requirements, appointments, and next steps.
* Maintain knowledge of community resources available throughout Fontana and surrounding communities.
* Work collaboratively with ESN staff to provide coordinated support instead of treating each program as a separate service.

Community Outreach

The Case Manager \& Partnership Coordinator will also represent Empowering Success Now throughout the community.

Responsibilities may include:

* Attend community outreach events, resource fairs, job fairs, networking events, workshops, and community meetings.
* Educate community members about ESN's programs and available services.
* Help identify individuals and families who may benefit from ESN services.
* Conduct outreach and assist potential clients with connecting to programs.
* Professionally represent ESN's mission and services when interacting with community members, businesses, organizations, and community leaders.
* Develop relationships with other organizations serving populations that may benefit from ESN programs.
* Help increase awareness, enrollment, participation, and successful completion across ESN programs.
